title: Earth and the Sky
seo_title: Year 2 Science: Earth and the Sky Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Recognise Earth is a planet in the solar system and identify patterns in the changing position of the Sun, Moon, planets and stars in the sky (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 2 science worksheets on Earth and the sky: Earth as a planet, day and night, the Sun's path, the Moon's changing shape, planets and stars, and the Southern Cross. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Earth spins to make day and night. The Moon changes shape over about a month.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth is a planet that goes around the Sun.

  • The Sun is a star.
  • Earth spins once a day: day and night.
  • The Moon goes around the Earth.
Example

Why is it night?

our side of Earth faces away from the Sun

Answer: Earth spins

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Sun moves around the Earth.
  • Thinking the Moon makes its own light.

faq.q: Why does the Sun seem to move across the sky?
faq.a: The Sun stays still. Earth spins, so the Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west.

faq.q: Why does the Moon change shape?
faq.a: The Moon is lit by the Sun. As it goes around the Earth, we see different amounts of the lit side.
It is a group of bright stars seen from Australia. It is on the Australian flag.
